workingDirectory.description: Where the brain runs — REQUIRED, never defaulted. It is the hire's blast radius: the brain reads and may write here, so a caller states it rather than inheriting the resident's own directory.

Required only when that precedent has already been surfaced to you and you are calling anyway; the reason is logged with the call. Never reaches the tool.

fullDiff.description: Default false: the response carries diffSummary (one row per file with its hunk and line counts) and the diff text capped at 24000 characters, setting truncated:true when it was cut. Set true for the whole diff — a 144-reference rename answered 167,785 characters, which a client could not display at all.

action.description: describe: 'next' takes the source units still to describe, 'done' records one as described, 'area' answers what the package a given file lives in is FOR — its area and the jobs inside it — and 'jobs_for' answers, for each member you name, the job the store ALREADY holds for it — in that job's own words, because a flag saying one exists cannot tell you whether the work in front of you is the same work — and lists the members that have none.

agent.description: transcript_append: what the agent said to him in the turn, verbatim.

budget_ms.description: recall/primer: the CALLER's deadline in milliseconds — state it when your own timeout is shorter than the 15s default, so a wedged store answers KNOWLEDGE_UNAVAILABLE inside your window instead of a transport timeout. Clamped: a caller may ask for a faster answer, never a longer wait.

bundle.description: describe action=done: which bundle the unit belongs to, for the coverage report. Omitted is a real state and is counted as 'unattributed' rather than folded into another bundle.

capture.description: transcript_append: 'turn' for a capture at a turn's end (default), 'compaction' for the catch-up taken before a compaction.

cause.description: record: the DIAGNOSIS — the underlying problem the solution addresses, distinct from the symptoms that reveal it. One symptom has many causes (a fast heartbeat: running, a heart attack, a virus) and the solution binds to the cause; when a symptom recall returns several entries, this field is what discriminates between them. Optional; never derived.

changedLines.description: describe action=jobs_for, with filePaths: the lines the caller WROTE, as an object from a file path (spelled as in filePaths) to a list of [first, last] line pairs, 1-based and inclusive. Only the methods those lines fall in — their Javadoc included — are asked about. A file with no entry, or an empty list, is asked about whole, which is the default: silence is never read as 'nothing was written'. Lines that fall in no method ask about nothing, and the call is refused rather than answered with an empty list.

client.description: transcript_append: the client that held the session.

confirm.description: wipe_and_import: REQUIRED true (wipes first). dedup: true = merge the groups.

contentHash.description: describe action=done: the contentHash action=next handed you WITH that unit. Required, and not re-read from the file on purpose — you described the text you were given, and recording today's text instead would claim a description nobody wrote and retire the unit for good.

days.description: prune: age threshold in days for rejected/superseded (default 30).

details.description: record: the longer story — including artifacts: paths, flags, ids and code references live HERE, not in symptoms.

entries.description: import: exported entries (inline alternative to path).

external_system.description: record: the external dependency, when the fault is external.

filePath.description: describe action=area: the source file whose package you want described. The package is derived through JDT rather than from the directory names, because which package a file declares is a fact about source roots that a path cannot be read for.

filePaths.description: describe action=jobs_for: source files whose members should be derived and asked about, instead of naming each member yourself. Needs a loaded project — which members a file declares is JDT's answer, and a caller parsing the file itself would be guessing. Without a project this REFUSES rather than answering that nothing is missing.

format.description: recall/primer/list: text = flat injection-ready lines; default json.

his.description: transcript_append: what he typed in the turn, verbatim.

id.description: promote: the entry id to re-status.

ids.description: delete: the entry ids to remove — exactly these and no others; a non-empty array, even for one id. promote_rule: the entry ids the rule is distilled from.

key.description: transcript_append: the client's own id for the record that opened the turn; the same for every capture of that turn, so a second capture completes the first. The store numbers the turns of a session itself.

kind.description: Which store operation: record (write) or recall (terminal retrieval).

lane.description: recall/nominate: REQUIRED (this or lanes) — which LIFECYCLE is searched, chosen BEFORE the search; a call naming no lane is refused. 'experience' (also 'lessons') is what happened in a situation: lessons and failure modes; 'patterns' is the borrowed catalogue of design patterns; 'domain' (also 'business') is what is true whoever reads it: facts, contracts, conventions; 'rules' are versioned and retired; 'code' says what each member and package is FOR, regenerated from the code it came from, and is asked only to check whether something already exists; 'transcript' is the discussion itself (what he typed, what the agent said to him, one line per tool call), asked with recall only, after a compaction, before something is attributed to him, or on demand, and never part of 'all'. Each lane is ranked and cut on its own and the answer says how many rows each searched. It is a FILTER, not a cue: give a cue as well.

lanes.description: recall/nominate: several lanes at once, by the same names as lane. Each is searched and ranked on its own.

language.description: record: anchor language (default java). Non-Java anchors (rust, ts, ...) are opaque to JDT maintenance — stored + recalled, never staled.

limit.description: primer: max domain nodes (default 20); list: max rows (default 50); describe action=next: max units to hand out (default 10) — this is the token budget for one describing pass.

links.description: record: typed edges [{rel, target}]. Allowed: applied | cured_by | derived_from | detected_by | fixed_by | handled_by | related | supersedes | undo. cured_by points at a jawata CAPABILITY rather than a code address (find_quality_issue(kind=…), seat:refactor) and is filled ONLY when the remedy needs no judgement — a cure WILL be run, and one that is right half the time is worse than none. A two-phase remedy (read the error, work out why, then decide) earns detected_by and no cure.

occasion.description: recall/nominate: the situation this call is made in, INSTEAD of lane / lanes (naming both is refused) — the engine answers which lanes that situation asks, so a client spells no lane. Occasions: typed_message (experience, rules); lesson_lookup (experience); tool_call (experience, code); recall_gate (experience, domain); after_compaction (transcript); design_question (experience, patterns); does_it_exist (code). Name one as occasion=<name>.

operation.description: record: operation this entry relates to. promote_rule: WHO the rule binds — seat:<name> for one seat, an activity label such as release, or all for every seat; required on a proposal (status=candidate).

package.description: recall: a package you are working in (cue).

path.description: load/wipe_and_import: a directory of *.md memory files, or a single file. Omit to use the configured default roots.

precedentOverride.description: Optional. One line saying why THIS case differs from a past call of this tool on this target that was reverted or errored. Required only when that precedent has already been surfaced to you and you are calling anyway; the reason is logged with the call. Never reaches the tool.

proceed_without_clean_backup.description: wipe, prune, import, delete, restore, wipe_and_import: the copy taken first is checked (its count must equal its rows) and tried 3 times; if it is still not clean the operation is REFUSED and nothing changes. Repeat the request with this set to true to go on anyway; one copy is still taken.

query_id.description: decide: the id the matching nominate call returned. It is required because a selection is only meaningful about the candidates it was offered — without it, any entry in the store could be returned as a vouched answer.

question.description: nominate: the question in your OWN WORDS, for the anchorless path — no symbol, no package, no operation. Say what you are trying to do. The answer comes back as RANKED CANDIDATES plus a query_id, never as a match: ranking is an ordering, not a claim that anything fits.

quote.description: transcript_verify: the words attributed to him.

recent.description: recall with lane=transcript alone: his most recent N messages, newest first, with the turn each came from. The thread to pick up after a compaction.

recursive.description: load/wipe_and_import: walk subdirectories of directory roots (default TRUE — the crawl finds everything; pass false to stay flat).

rule_lifecycle_note.description: NOT AN INPUT — the rule verbs, said once. promote_rule(ids, summary[, situation]) distils entries into a RULE at version 1, linked derived_from each source; the sources are NOT superseded and go on answering as themselves. amend_rule(id, summary) writes a NEW version and supersedes the old one, which stays readable — what a rule USED to say is what a version number is for. retire_rule(id) records that it stopped applying, as of now: recall stops offering it, list and get still answer. Retiring is not rejecting and not superseding — the rule was right, nothing replaced it, and it stopped applying.

scope.description: list: symbol/package prefix filter. describe action=next: the package to describe, including its subpackages; omit for the whole workspace.

seats.description: review_sweep: the directory holding the seat files. Lists, under rulesNobodyAsks, the accepted rules whose operation label no seat or activity asks for, so a typo in a label is reported rather than silently binding nothing.

selected_ids.description: decide: the candidate ids you judged APPLICABLE, after reading each one's situation. An EMPTY list is a real answer and often the right one — it records that nothing applied, which is what the store previously could not say. Ids the nomination did not offer are refused, not ignored.

situation.description: record: WHEN this applies. A situation is a GREP, a TASK, or a NUMBER. A grep — something you can look up in the code in front of you: "when a test class declares @BeforeAll or @AfterAll". A task — what you are doing right now: "when amending an order that is already partially filled". A number — a value you can read off an output: "when a test run reports a class-level exception count above zero". If it is none of the three it describes how the system works, which is true during every call and tells no one whether this entry is for them. Never a package or a symbol: a location matches everything inside it and distinguishes nothing. REQUIRED for lesson and failure_mode.

status.description: record: default candidate. promote_rule: candidate (a proposal, injected nowhere until he accepts it with kind=promote) or accepted (the default).

summary.description: record: ONE judgeable sentence of experience — what was learned, stated so a later reader can judge whether it transfers. Not a heading, not a title (a heading-shaped summary is refused). A story owes: situation (When does this apply?); summary (What happened, or what to do?); details (Why, and what would a reader do differently?); outcome (How did it turn out?); anchor (Which code, if any?). REFUSED outright, whatever the type: empty, fallback slip, log line, compaction artifact, status note, section heading, not a claim — a log records that something happened, an experience says what to DO about it, and project progress was true when written and is false now.

surface.description: recall: which surface is asking — 'seat' when a driven seat run recalls, omitted for an ordinary question. Affects only the quality counters (stats), never what is retrieved.

symbol.description: record: anchor FQN (mutually exclusive with packages/symbols).

symptom.description: recall: an observed symptom / cue phrase (alias-normalized).

symptoms.description: record: how the problem LOOKED — each item a prose observation in words. NOT paths, flags, tags, code symbols or headings (refused with a redirect): artifacts belong in 'details', symbols in 'symbol'/'symbols', tool output in the tool lane, which the tools record themselves.

tools.description: transcript_append: one line per tool call (tool, key argument, ok or failed). Never tool output.

ts.description: transcript_append: when the turn ended, ISO-8601 (default: now).

type.description: record: entry type (domain_fact / lesson / failure_mode / api_contract / naming_convention / ...).

unit.description: describe action=done: the unit path action=next handed you.

verdict.description: record: how it turned out. REQUIRED for lesson and failure_mode — for those the outcome IS the lesson. Use 'unproven' when it genuinely has not been settled; that is an answer, and inventing a verdict is not.
